common_name: Wanda Daylily (Historic Parent of Red Ribbons)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring or early fall in average, well-drained soil in full sun; established clumps need only routine watering and periodic division.

directions: Wanda is a historic Hemerocallis cultivar documented chiefly as one of the two parents, crossed with Mabel Fuller, behind G.A. Lenington's 1964 introduction Red Ribbons, a tall spider-form daylily that went on to win the American Hemerocallis Society's Harris Olson Spider Award along with Honorable Mention and Award of Merit honors. No detailed record of Wanda's own flower color or form survives in the sources consulted, a common gap for mid-twentieth-century parent cultivars overshadowed by their award-winning offspring. Grow it, as with other mid-century diploid daylilies, in average, well-drained soil in full sun, dividing congested clumps every three to four years to maintain vigorous flowering.

common_name: Priscilla's Rainbow Daylily (Tetraploid Parent of Magnificent Rainbow)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring or early fall in average, well-drained soil in full sun; divide congested clumps every three to four years to sustain bloom.

directions: Priscilla's Rainbow is a tetraploid Hemerocallis cultivar documented as one of the two parents, crossed with Always Afternoon, behind Patrick Stamile's 1995 introduction Magnificent Rainbow, a large-flowered lavender bicolor that itself later helped produce the Candy-series cultivar Huckleberry Candy. Beyond its tetraploid status and this breeding role, no further description of its own flower color or form survives in the sources consulted. Grow it, as with other modern tetraploid daylilies, in full sun in average, well-drained soil, dividing congested clumps every three to four years to sustain vigorous bloom.
